To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transmission matrix of a multiple-scattering sample can be used to enhance nonlinear fluorescence processes, such as two-photon exciation fluorescence, and to achieve high-contrast imaging through the sample.

we have developed and compared several matrix approaches to enhance two-photon fluorescence through multiple scattering media, and that we have demonstrated that these techniques can be used to perform point scanning fluorescence imaging of fluorescent microbeads at depths where conventional imaging would fail because of multiple scattering effects.
we have shown the possibility of enhancing two-photon fluorescence excitation through thick scattering media by using transmission matrix approaches.

the control of the nonlinear optical response of a fluorescent object located after a scattering medium.
the use of multiple scattering media to enhance nonlinear optical processes.
the development of new methods for controlling light propagation through multiple-scattering media.
